title: Thermoplastics and thermosets
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers chain length, branching, packing and cross-links together, so it is broader than the new point's single contrast between thermoplastics and thermosets, and it does not name thermoplastics or thermosets.

draft.title: Thermoplastics and thermosets
card: The polymer chains are not joined to each other by covalent bonds. Only weak forces hold neighbouring chains together.
Strong covalent bonds, called cross-links, join the chains into one network. The cross-links hold the chains in place.
Heating a thermoplastic weakens the forces between chains, so the chains slide past each other. The plastic softens and can be reshaped, then sets again as it cools.
Heating a thermoset does not let its chains slide, as the cross-links hold them. It stays rigid, and strong heating breaks down the polymer instead of softening it.
draft.remember: Thermoplastic: no cross-links, so it softens. Thermoset: cross-linked, so it stays rigid.

a.q: Why can a thermoplastic be softened and reshaped by heating?
opts: Its chains are not cross-linked, so they can slide
Its chains are joined by strong covalent cross-links
Its chains are all much shorter than thermoset chains
Its chains break into monomers when they are heated
a.why: With no cross-links, only weak forces hold the chains, so heating lets them slide. Cross-links are the feature of thermosets, which is why that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what holds neighbouring chains together.

b.q: A kettle handle stays rigid and does not soften near hot steam. Which explanation best fits this?
opts: Cross-links between chains hold them in place
Weak forces let its chains slide past each other
Its chains have no bonds between them at all
It was made from monomers with no double bonds
b.why: A handle that stays rigid when hot suggests a thermoset, whose cross-links stop chains sliding. Weak forces between chains would let it soften.
b.clue: Which type does not soften with heat?

a.best: Its chains are not cross-linked, so they can slide

b.best: Cross-links between chains hold them in place
